 2028 FERS, CSRS and Social Security COLA Estimate
 November 10, 2026 My Federal Retirement 
 The Senior Citizens League (TSCL) issued its first prediction for the 2028 Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) on November 10, 2026: 3.6%.
 It is the first TSCL estimate since the official 2027 COLA was announced last month, and it matches that 2027 increase of 3.6% for Social Security and Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS) annuitants.
 Get an email alert when the 2028 Federal Retiree COLA is officially announced 
 Join the free newsletter to get an alert when new 2028 COLA estimates are released for CSRS, FERS, and Social Security.
 TSCL’s First 2028 COLA Prediction
 TSCL, a nonpartisan seniors’ advocacy group, updates its COLA forecast each month with a statistical model built on the Consumer Price Index (CPI), the Federal Reserve interest rate, and the national unemployment rate. The group also released a new version of that model (v1.3) this month, which it says updates the date-processing and data-cleaning steps and slightly improves predictive accuracy.
 The 2028 COLA will be based on the average Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) for July, August, and September 2027, compared with the same three months of 2026. The Social Security Administration (SSA) is expected to announce the official figure in October 2027, after the September inflation report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics .

 What 3.6% Would Mean for CSRS and FERS Retirees
 If the 2028 COLA ends up at 3.6%, the three groups would not receive the same increase:
 Social Security: 3.6%
 CSRS: 3.6%
 FERS: 2.6%, because the FERS COLA is reduced by one percentage point whenever the Social Security COLA is above 3%
 The 2027 COLA followed the same pattern, with CSRS and Social Security at 3.6% and FERS at 2.6%. The Guide to Federal Retiree COLAs explains how the FERS formula works and who qualifies for it, and What NARFE Wants Congress to Do About the FERS COLA Gap covers the legislative effort to change it.
 Why a Year-Ahead Estimate Is Early
 None of the data that determines the 2028 COLA exists yet. TSCL’s early-2026 predictions for the 2027 COLA ran between 2.5% and 2.8%, and energy-driven inflation pushed the official figure to 3.6%. A first estimate in November is best read as a starting point that will move with inflation, energy prices, and the other factors in the model over the next 11 months.
 What TSCL Is Asking the Next Congress to Do
 TSCL used the release to call on the incoming Congress to take up several benefit issues. It cited projections that Social Security faces automatic benefit reductions in 2032 and that the Medicare Part A trust fund becomes insolvent in 2033. TSCL’s requests include:
 Lifting or eliminating the Social Security payroll tax threshold, which is $184,500 in 2026
 Restoring Medicare and Medicaid budget cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill
 Adding dental, vision, and hearing coverage to Medicare
 Issuing a one-time $1,400 stimulus payment to seniors
 TSCL Executive Director Shannon Benton said benefits reform can happen even when two different parties control Washington. More details are on the TSCL COLA Watch page .
 What to Watch Next
 Monthly CPI-W reports from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, which drive each new TSCL update
 First 2028 estimates from AARP, Mary Johnson, and CRFB
 The official announcement from the Social Security Administration in October 2027
